access_links.label: EU-wide stress testing page (methodology, templates, results)

description: The EU-wide stress test is the European Banking Authority's recurring exercise to assess how large EU banks' capital would hold up under an adverse macroeconomic scenario, with a common methodology, scenarios, templates and published bank-level results. It is run by the EBA with the European Systemic Risk Board, which designs the adverse scenario, the European Central Bank and the European Commission. The 2027 exercise, whose draft methodology was released for industry consultation in June 2026, covers 63 banks from the EU and Norway, 47 of them in the euro area, about 75% of EU banking assets, and for the first time integrates climate risk while simplifying the method. The page offers the methodological note, template guidance and Excel templates, and earlier exercises publish results per bank, free of charge. Caveats: scenarios are hypothetical, and banks project their own results under constraints, so outcomes are not forecasts; the page read gives no reuse licence. For simulation it provides scenario paths and bank-level capital data for resilience and cascading failure models of the financial system, and a template for adding physical and climate shocks to infrastructure financing. It is related to the Federal Reserve stress test scenarios record in this catalogue, the US equivalent.
